# Temple Scroll Column 61 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 61:1 — "give" vs. "deliver" vs. "hand over" — נתן in military context

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "give them into your hand" | Literal rendering of נתן + ביד |
| LOGOS | "deliver them into your hand" | Formal military register |
| PNEUMA | "hand them over to you" | Natural modern English idiom |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "deliver." Maintains biblical register while being clear; EMET's "give" is too flat for military context; PNEUMA's "hand over" is too colloquial.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 61:4 — "a full month of days" vs. "a full month" vs. "an entire month"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a full month of days" | Literal Hebrew construct ירח ימים |
| LOGOS | "a full month" | Standard English equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "an entire month" | Emphatic modern phrasing |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "a full month." EMET's "month of days" is a Hebraism unnecessary in English; PNEUMA's "entire" slightly shifts emphasis.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 61:7 — "deal tyrannically" vs. "treat as a slave" vs. "exploit" — תתעמר

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "deal tyrannically with her" | Preserves the rare verb form's force |
| LOGOS | "treat her as a slave" | Clarifies the practical meaning |
| PNEUMA | "exploit her" | Modern equivalent capturing the power dynamic |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "treat her as a slave." The verb תתעמר specifically connotes treating as merchandise/chattel; LOGOS captures this while EMET is vague and PNEUMA too general.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 61:8 — "hated" vs. "unloved" vs. "does not love" — שנואה

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "hated" | Literal rendering of שנואה |
| LOGOS | "unloved" | Formal English equivalent avoiding hyperbole |
| PNEUMA | "does not love" | Periphrastic, accessible |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "unloved." Hebrew שנואה in marital context means "less loved" rather than literal hatred; LOGOS captures this nuance. PNEUMA's periphrasis is too wordy for repeated use.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 61:12 — "beginning of his strength" vs. "first fruit of his vigor" vs. "first sign of his father's strength"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the beginning of his strength" | Literal ראשית אונו |
| LOGOS | "the first fruit of his vigor" | Elevated formal register |
| PNEUMA | "the first sign of his father's strength" | Clarifies referent with "father's" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted hybrid "first fruit of his strength." LOGOS's "vigor" is unnecessarily archaic; EMET's "beginning" loses the firstfruits imagery; PNEUMA's added "father's" is explanatory but not in the text.

**Status:** Resolved with compromise.

---

## 61:15 — "glutton and drunkard" vs. "wastrel and drunk" — זולל וסובא

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a glutton and a drunkard" | Traditional biblical pair |
| LOGOS | "a glutton and a drunkard" | Standard scholarly rendering |
| PNEUMA | "a wastrel and a drunk" | "Wastrel" captures dissolute character |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET/LOGOS "a glutton and a drunkard." This is the recognized biblical phrase (cf. Deut 21:20, Prov 23:21). PNEUMA's "wastrel" is creative but departs from the established rendering.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---
